# Haritacajātaka (Ja 431)

**ID:** Ja 431
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Haritacajātaka
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** The Ascetic Goldskin

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Haritacajātaka* (Ja 431), also titled *Hāritajātaka*, is a canonical birth-story preserved in the Pali Jātaka collection [Fausböll 1897; SuttaCentral]. According to the frame narrative, the Buddha delivers the story while residing at Jetavana to admonish a discontented monk who, agitated by the sight of a beautiful, smartly attired woman, neglected his appearance and contemplated leaving the monastic life [SuttaCentral]. In the story of the past, an ascetic who has mastered the five psychic faculties and eight meditative attainments loses his powers after being overcome by passion for a queen [Ānandajoti 2010; SuttaCentral]. When subsequently questioned by the king, the ascetic refuses to tell a falsehood—observing that one who forsakes the truth cannot attain awakening—and truthfully admits his fault [Ānandajoti 2010; Appleton 2010]. Verses associated with the text illustrate moral maxims, emphasizing that it is unacceptable for a wise person to succumb to anger, just as an unrestrained monk, a lazy layman, or an inconsiderate king fall short [Ānandajoti 2010].

In discussions of Buddhist ethics and the Bodhisatta's cultivation of the perfections (*pāramitā*), the prose of the *Hāritajātaka* is famously cited to illustrate the perfection of truthfulness (*sacca*): it states that across his countless past lives, the Bodhisatta might under certain circumstances violate the other moral precepts, but he will never break his commitment to truth by uttering an untruth [Appleton 2010; Nārada 2008].

SuttaCentral notes four translations into four languages [SuttaCentral]. In terms of text reuse, DharmaNexus identifies 11 Pali-internal matches between the canonical text and the prose *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (matching 911 characters, notably §7.1–7.4 with §4503–4506) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records low-scoring automatic cross-language alignments with the Tibetan version of the *Pitāputrasamāgamana-sūtra* (D0060), though these remain machine alignments without verified parallel status [DharmaNexus].

- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā (Tatiyo bhāgo) (Atk S0513a3) (§7.1–7.4 ↔ §4503–4506)
- Cross-language matches (DharmaNexus): འཕགས་པ་ཡབ་དང་སྲས་མཇལ་བ་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ཐེག་པ་ཆེན་པོའི་མདོ (ārya-pitāputrasamāgamana-nāma-mahāyānasūtra) (D0060) [bo]

- [Appleton 2010] Naomi Appleton, Jātaka Stories in Theravāda Buddhism: Narrating the Bodhisatta Path (2010) — Discusses the Bodhisatta's interior monologue on truthfulness and the famous principle that the Bodhisatta never lies despite violating other precepts.

- [Nārada 2008] Nārada Mahāthera, The Buddha and His Teachings (Revised 2008) — Notes the citation of Ja 431 regarding the Bodhisatta's perfection of truthfulness.
